title: A Voice Memo About Choosing Silence Over Gossip
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Something happened at work today that I keep replaying in my mind, so I wanted to record my thoughts before I forget how it felt.
Narrator: [honest] During lunch, two coworkers started talking about Rina, our new manager, saying she only got promoted because she's close friends with the director.
Narrator: [reflective] I don't actually know if that's true, and honestly, neither do they, although they spoke about it as though it were completely certain.
Narrator: [tempted] Part of me wanted to join the conversation, because I had noticed a few strange decisions Rina made during her first month leading our team.
Narrator: [thoughtful] But then I remembered how gossip spreads so quickly, changing slightly with every person who repeats it, until it barely resembles the truth anymore.
Narrator: [honestly] So instead of adding my own opinion, I simply said I didn't know enough about the situation to comment on it fairly.
Narrator: [determined] After lunch, I actually went to talk with Rina directly about one decision that had confused me during her first weeks.
Narrator: [warmly] She explained her reasoning clearly, and honestly, it made much more sense once I understood the full situation behind it.
Narrator: [reflective] If I had simply gossiped about her instead, I would still be confused, and she would never have known that people were talking about her at all.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I used to think staying out of gossip made me boring, or somehow distant from my coworkers and their daily conversations.
Narrator: [honestly] Now I think it just means I'd rather build real understanding than spread stories that might not even be true in the first place.
Narrator: [gently] Words travel so much faster than the truth sometimes, especially once they leave our mouths and enter someone else's conversation.
Narrator: [peacefully] Tonight, I feel proud of a very small, quiet choice that nobody else at work will probably ever notice or remember.
Narrator: [warmly] I'm turning off this recording now, but I hope tomorrow, when I'm tempted again, I remember how good today's silence actually felt.

options: She said she didn't know enough about the situation to comment fairly
quiz.explanation: She said she didn't know enough about the situation to comment on it fairly.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do after lunch?
options: She went to talk with Rina directly about a decision that confused her
She told Rina about the gossip
quiz.explanation: She went to talk with Rina directly about one decision that had confused her.

options: It makes her boring and distant

quiz.explanation: She concludes she'd rather build real understanding than spread stories that might not even be true.
